chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man whom a group of people had instructed to buy a camel for them with cash, and they would give him extra for deferment (credit). So he bought a camel for them, and one of them was with him. He (peace be upon him) forbade him to take from them extra above his cash price for the deferment.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on adding extra value to a cash price for credit deferment?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that the additional compensation for the delay in payment (the 'credit premium') must be kept separate from the principal debt to prevent it from being treated as interest (riba) if the buyer defaults. This distinction is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for validating credit sales (bay' al-ta'jil) while ensuring the extra amount remains a voluntary gift or fee rather than an automatic increase in the debt obligation.
